title: Entropy-aware KV packing and background scrub playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Investigate, prototype, and implement an entropy-aware allocation strategy for the KV cache combined with a low-priority background scrub/rewrite controller to reduce long-term fragmentation and improve memory packing on GPUs. The goal is to reduce tail latency and OOM incidents under mixed-length continuous batching workloads while preserving SLOs and minimizing CPU/GPU overhead.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator adds an entropy score per allocation region and prefers insertions into low-entropy zones (measured by key access distribution and average active TTL)
Background scrub controller can rewrite and repack >60% of fragmented slots per GPU per hour without exceeding a 5% CPU budget or increasing 99th percentile latency by more than 3ms
End-to-end e2e benchmark shows at least 18% reduction in peak GPU memory usage and a 20% reduction in periodic OOM/eviction events on production-like mixed sequence workloads
Feature includes metrics + dashboards for fragmentation heatmap, rewrite throughput, entropy distribution, and scrub budget consumption
Can roll back to previous allocation policy via rollout flags within two deployment cycles (canary and full rollout)
technical_notes: Entropy metric: combine per-slot hit frequency histogram (last N minutes) and TTL variance to compute normalized entropy in [0,1]; lower entropy => more predictable, better packing candidate
Allocation policy: prefer placing new KV slabs into contiguous low-entropy regions; if not available, use ephemeral micro-reserve pool followed by background rewrite to compact

Background scrub: staged rewrite controller with three priority bins (idle, low, maintenance). Idle scraps run only when GPU kernel queue depth is under threshold; low runs during normal operation within budget; maintenance runs during off-peak windows
Integration with continuous batching: scrub controller listens to real-time batch-size and latency SLO signals; it throttles or pauses scrubs when serving latency exceeds configured guardrails

Memory packing optimizations: align slab sizes to warp-friendly boundaries, co-locate small keys to reduce padding waste, and prefer 4K-aligned contiguous regions for mapped GPU memory to reduce TLB pressure
Safety: atomic rewrite uses copy-on-write metadata switch; scrub controller performs per-shard checksums and can abort/rollback partial rewrites on mismatch
Telemetry: add per-GPU fragmentation_heat, scrub_ops_total, scrub_time_ms, entropy_distribution_percentiles, micro_reserve_utilization metrics
Bench harness: extend existing perf-suite with mixed-length seq distributions and real prefix reuse traces from anonymized production logs (sanitized)
Trade-offs: aggressive repacking reduces fragmentation but increases transient memory pressure and kernel churn; default config is conservative, tunable per-customer

decisions: Use combined hit-frequency + TTL variance as the entropy signal rather than pure LRU recency — better separation between hot predictable items and cold churn
Prefer conservative default scrubbing parameters (low priority ops) and make aggressive modes opt-in via config for Dedicated customers
Atomic switch strategy for rewrites to avoid lock-heavy moves; rely on copy-on-write plus checksum validation
Expose per-customer knobs in Dedicated/Private for scrub budget and micro-reserve size; hosted API will use tuned defaults
